There's a key detail in the new Apple Upgrade Program: "If you are obtaining your iPhone via a lease, you are required to connect with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon at signup."

John Gruber of Daring Fireball published an article this morning offering a possible explanation for this requirement.

Apple Upgrade iPhone Restrictions

According to an email provided to Gruber by a former employee of Apple's carrier team, this requirement stems primarily from agreements Apple has made with Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile in the United States.

The contracts negotiated with each of these carriers are worth "hundreds of millions of dollars," and Apple makes concessions in exchange for these payments. Requiring iPhones purchased through Apple Upgrade to be linked to a T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T account is one such concession.

The former Apple employee further explained the details of these agreements:

On the other hand, this also involves fraud and risk assessment. Another former Apple Store retail employee told Gruber that since Apple began offering carrier installment plans in its retail stores, fraudulent iPhone sales have "dramatically increased."

Apple does note that while you need to connect your iPhone to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when signing up for Apple Upgrade, the phone itself remains unlocked: "iPhones obtained via a lease are required to select a qualified carrier (prepaid carrier plans are not eligible). Leased iPhones remain unlocked at all times, so you may switch to another carrier at any time, subject to that carrier's terms."

Gruber's full article is available on Daring Fireball.
